answer: Each identity runs a garden lagoon station and locks 75 bonds. A lantern shines through a lagoon sample, and the identity files the photometer reading with the serials. An auditor recomputes the reading from the lantern-lumen and lagoon turbidity tables, burning the bond on drift over 3 percent, a repeated serial, or a shared offset. First costs 37, the kth 37 plus 7 times k minus 1, the 1000th 7030; 1000 fakes pay 3,535,500 plus 75,000 locked. A rented-photometer ring fails: its shared offset appears under many serials at once. An honest keeper pays 37 once, reclaiming the bond after audit.
